stem: During a follow-up consultation, a 16-year-old is trying to balance school, sport, casual work, and future study plans; which consultation approach best matches adolescent cognitive development?

options.text: Direct almost all discussion to the parents because adolescents are not yet ready for abstract reasoning
Keep the discussion concrete only and avoid asking about future consequences or alternative options
Ask the young person to weigh several options, think ahead, and help problem-solve the next steps
Avoid involving the young person in planning until adulthood because future planning is not part of adolescent development
Focus only on current emotions because multidimensional thinking is not expected until after adolescence

explanation: Adolescent cognitive development includes abstract thinking, future planning, and problem-solving, so involving the young person in weighing options and planning next steps is the best approach.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because adolescents are developing the capacity for abstract reasoning and should not be excluded from consultation and planning.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adolescent development includes the ability to consider future consequences and alternative options.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because this approach uses emerging abstract thinking, future planning, and problem-solving in a developmentally appropriate way.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because future planning is part of normal adolescent cognitive development, not something deferred until adulthood.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because adolescents are capable of more than current-emotion focus, including multidimensional and forward-looking thinking.
